# D.3.7: reversible classes generated by abelian Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces

## Result and scope

The complete proof is `sections/D3_abelian.tex`. Every abelian `K(A,n)`, n >= 1, has the same reversible aspherical closure as a subset of the countable list

`BQ, K(Z_(p),n), K(F_p,n), K(C_(p infinity),n)`.

Allowing all n still gives a single countable list. Arbitrary classes of connected GEM generators therefore reduce to a subset of that list, hence to one countable CW generator. They are accessible by B.4, and there are at most continuum many, including after restricting to any fixed stable part. The general fixed-stable-part set-size question remains open: no assertion says arbitrary reversible localizers are GEM-generated.

For nonzero torsion-free A the sharper equality is Rev K(A,n) = Rev K(Z[J^-1],n), J = {p : pA=A}. For nonzero p-primary torsion A, ordinary nullity is K(Cp-infinity,n) when divisible and K(Fp,n) otherwise. No uniqueness or irredundancy of the general normal forms is asserted.

## Primary texts opened and exact uses

1. Don Stanley, *Invariants of t-structures and classification of nullity classes*, arXiv:math/0602252v1 (12 February 2006), Section 8, Theorems 8.2 and 8.5, pages 25--26 of the PDF. URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0602252 . The source supplies the rigid-abelian ordinary-nullity construction being examined, not its reversible analogue.
2. A. K. Bousfield, *Homotopical localizations of spaces*, AJM 119 (1997), 1321--1354. URL: https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/bous1.pdf . Beginning of Section 5, p.1330: acyclic pointed spaces are closed under homotopy colimits and fibre extensions. Section 5.6, p.1331: Ext-complete groups satisfy Hom(Q,-)=Ext(Q,-)=0. Lemma 9.13, p.1344: each K(Fp,n) is either local or acyclic for any localization. The latter dichotomy, combined with nonzero Hom(A,Fp), proves the nondivisible p-torsion case uniformly for n=1 as well.
3. A. K. Bousfield, *Unstable localization and periodicity* (1996). URL: https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/bousfield-ulp.pdf . Section 4, p.41, immediately after Theorem 4.1: Ext(Cp-infinity,F)=lim F/p^kF when p-torsion is bounded. Only the torsion-free case is used in D.3.7.

## Adversarial checks and repaired interfaces

- **No arbitrary product closure.** The sum-to-product quotient for the prime components is a Q-vector space, proved by the snake lemma separately at every prime. Both its kernel and cokernel of multiplication by a fixed prime are controlled by the one corresponding coordinate.
- **Degree n=1.** Rational-cokernel inclusions of abelian groups induce mod-l homology equivalences by the Serre spectral sequence with trivial monodromy. Their cofibers have uniquely divisible integral homology and rational suspension spectra. We do not claim that a disconnected rational homotopy fibre is in the rational null class.
- **No separatedness assumption for the Ext group.** For a reduced A, C_p=Ext(Cp-infinity,A) is a Zp-module with Hom(Q,C_p)=Ext(Q,C_p)=0, directly from derived tensor--Hom adjunction. C_p can have torsion and need not be separated in its ordinary p-adic topology. Separation is used only for the completion of its torsion-free quotient.
- **Torsion-free quotient.** F=C_p/tor(C_p) has Ext(Q,F)=0 by global dimension one. Its exact completion sequence has rational kernel and zero cokernel; the rational kernel is injective, so it splits. If F/pF is nonzero, the completed-free description gives a projection onto Zp.
- **Completed free versus abstract free.** A torsion-free separated p-complete module is the completion of a free Zp-module on lifts of a mod-p basis. It need not be abstractly free. The reverse nullity implication uses a separate abstract free resolution of length one over the PID Zp.
- **Actual realization of quotient.** For 0 -> F1 -> F0 -> M -> 0, the bar homotopy quotient of K(F0,n) by K(F1,n) has exactly M in degree n. Its simplicial terms are finite products of spaces already ordinary-acyclic. No arbitrary fibre two-out-of-three rule is used.
- **Splitting a Zp quotient.** Every additive h:M -> Zp from a Zp-module is Zp-linear, by integer approximation modulo p^k and separatedness of the target. A surjection therefore splits after choosing a lift of 1. No continuity or topology on M is assumed.
- **Countable replacement.** Zp/Z_(p) is a Q-vector space. Thus only countable groups remain after adjoining the rational class. The universal list and its arbitrary subwedges have countable simplicial/CW models.

Root and the independent `fibrations_groups` agent reviewed the algebraic interfaces before integration. Their suggested n=1 correction is included in the full proof.

## PolyGEM extension and interval consequence

The independent simple_higher agent identified the exact extension: Chacholski--Dror Farjoun--Flores--Scherer, GT19 (2015) 2741--2766, Proposition 6.2(4) compares ordinary acyclic classes of a polyGEM X and its free abelian construction ZX (the overlined C notation is defined in Section 2). Proposition 5.2 puts connected nilpotent finite Postnikov pieces among polyGEMs. We and root independently opened the primary PDF and its proof. The countable-list theorem therefore extends to arbitrary classes of connected polyGEM generators. No inverse-limit closure is used. URL: https://msp.org/gt/2015/19-5/gt-v19-n5-p07-p.pdf .

The unnumbered interval consequence uses the independently opened Levy2025 Theorem3.2: all connected infinite-loop generators whose reduced suspension spectra lie in loc(S/p) are already ordinary BZ/p-acyclic. Thus a reversible localizer generated by these spaces, or by connected polyGEMs, cannot strictly interpolate between minRev(BZ/p) and Rloc(S/p). This does not exclude intermediate localizers with genuinely nonlinear generators.
